fields.name: Maṇīndracandra Nandī (Mahārāja of Kāśimbāzār)
fields.notes: Mahārāja of Kāśimbāzār (1860-1929); humble and generous to the Vaiṣṇava cause: temples, holy places, lost books recovered; walked barefoot in nagara-saṅkīrtana; published the Bhāgavatam with Bengali translation. Moved to serve the Vaiṣṇavas by Rāmacandra dāsa Bābājī of Jaṅgīpur (#1239).
The courtesan paid a lakh by Rāmacandra Khān of Benāpola (#1245) to break Haridāsa Ṭhākura's sādhana; by Haridāsa's influence she became a devout Vaiṣṇavī (Kṛṣṇadāsī).

fields.place: Cuttack (Orissa); edicts at Purī, Bhubaneswar, Kūrmadeva (Ganjam)
fields.notes: Founder of the Gajapati house of Orissa (1435-1470, capital Cuttack), father of Puruṣottama Deva (#1131); his edicts at Purī order Jagannātha's utensils, ornaments, Āndhra dances and the recitation of the Gīta-govinda.

fields.works: Gaura-vinodinī vṛtti (on the Śikṣāṣṭaka); Gaura-gītā; some 4,000 padas in Vrajabuli; the Gīta-govinda in Vrajabuli verse; Padakalpataru 1844
fields.notes: Rāma Rāya Gosvāmī, of the family of a disciple of Nityānanda and of Jayadeva's line; commentary on the Śikṣāṣṭaka, the Gaura-gītā, 4,000 Vrajabuli padas; named in Nābhājī's Bhaktamāla; descendants at Bihārīpaḍā, Vṛndāvana. A pada of the Padakalpataru (1844) bears his name.

Disciple of Candraśekhara Vaidya of Kāśī, in whose house the Lord taught Sanātana; after his guru's death kept and served the place, and showed Śrīnivāsa and Narottama the places of the Lord's pastimes (Prema-vilāsa 10).

fields.name: Kutubuddīn (dacoit)
fields.notes: A Muslim dacoit chief who tried to rob Jāhnavā-devī's party on her way to Vṛndāvana; by her power they wandered all night, and at dawn he took shelter at her feet (Prema-vilāsa 9).

Disciple of Pūjārī Ṭhākura; settled in Vṛndāvana; with Rāmadāsa, disciple of Bhūgarbha Ṭhākura, sent by Jīva and Lokanātha Gosvāmī by Kheturī, Yājigrāma and Gopīvallabhapura to bring news of Narottama, Śrīnivāsa and Śyāmānanda (Prema-vilāsa 17). Taken out of the record «Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Others» #1888 (07-11-2026).

fields.guru: The descendants of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya at Mālihāṭī
fields.notes: A wealthy Faujdār and once a Tantric; through his Vaiṣṇava wife became a devotee and took guidance from Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's descendants at Mālihāṭī (Bhaktamāla 17); his Deity Nandadulāla is at Kiśoranagara-Jālālapura.

Father of Mādhavācārya, husband of Nityānanda's daughter Gaṅgā; friend of Bhagīratha Ācārya, whose wife Jayadurgā raised his son when he took sannyāsa and settled at Kāśī (Prema-vilāsa 21). Divākara (the sun-god) in Kṛṣṇa-līlā (GGD 113).

Grandson of Cakrapāṇi Caudhurī of Śrīkhaṇḍa (circle of Raghunandana Ṭhākura); grandfather of Madana (Bengali Govinda-līlāmṛta) and of Rāmagopāla (#1265, Rasa-kalpavallī), whose son Pītāmbara wrote the Rasa-mañjarī.
